state_analysis: The analysis_report.txt file has been created successfully. Now I need to create the optimized_logrotate.conf file with proper rotation configurations for all log files.
explanation: Creating the optimized_logrotate.conf file with proper rotation schedules, compression settings, and retention policies for all log files.

commands.keystrokes:
cat > /app/optimized_logrotate.conf << 'EOF'
# Optimized Logrotate Configuration
# Generated by Log Rotation Analyzer
# 
# This configuration addresses the following issues:
# - Missing rotation for error.log and debug.log
# - Inadequate rotation frequency for access.log
# - Suboptimal rotation for app.log
# - Compliance requirements (PCI-DSS, SOX)
#
# Rotation scheduled to run at 03:00 (off-peak hours)
# Peak traffic hours avoided: 09:00-11:00, 14:00-16:00, 20:00-22:00

#============================================================================
# APPLICATION LOG - High volume, 30-day retention required
#============================================================================
/var/log/samples/app.log {
    # Rotation schedule: Daily to manage 125.3 MB/day growth
    daily
    
    # Retention: 30 copies for 30-day compliance requirement
    rotate 30
    
    # Compression settings
    compress
    compresscmd /usr/bin/gzip
    compressoptions -9
    delaycompress
    
    # Size-based rotation trigger (rotate if size exceeds threshold)
    # Prevents runaway growth during traffic spikes
    maxsize 200M
    
    # Minimum size to rotate (don't rotate tiny files)
    minsize 1M
    
    # Handle missing files gracefully
    missingok
    
    # Don't rotate empty files
    notifempty
    
    # Create new file with proper permissions
    create 644 www-data www-data
    
    # Use date extension for easier identification
    dateext
    dateformat -%Y%m%d
    
    # Post-rotation script (signal application to reopen logs)
    postrotate
        # Send HUP signal to application if it has a PID file
        [ -f /var/run/app.pid ] && kill -HUP $(cat /var/run/app.pid) 2>/dev/null || true
    endscript
}

#============================================================================
# ACCESS LOG - Medium-high volume, 14-day retention required
#============================================================================
/var/log/samples/access.log {
    # Rotation schedule: Daily to manage 45.7 MB/day growth
    # Changed from monthly - monthly was allowing 1.4GB accumulation!
    daily
    
    # Retention: 14 copies for 14-day requirement
    rotate 14
    
    # Compression settings
    compress
    compresscmd /usr/bin/gzip
    compressoptions -9
    delaycompress
    
    # Size-based rotation trigger
    maxsize 100M
    
    # Minimum size to rotate
    minsize 1M
    
    # Handle edge cases
    missingok
    notifempty
    
    # Create new file with proper permissions (nginx owner)
    create 644 www-data www-data
    
    # Use date extension
    dateext
    dateformat -%Y%m%d
    
    # Post-rotation script for nginx
    postrotate
        # Signal nginx to reopen log files
        [ -f /var/run/nginx.pid ] && kill -USR1 $(cat /var/run/nginx.pid) 2>/dev/null || true
    endscript
}

#============================================================================
# ERROR LOG - CRITICAL: Previously had NO rotation config!
# Compliance-critical (PCI-DSS, SOX), 60-day retention required
#============================================================================
/var/log/samples/error.log {
    # Rotation schedule: Weekly (8.9 MB/day = ~62 MB/week, manageable)
    weekly
    
    # Retention: 9 copies for 63 days (exceeds 60-day requirement)
    rotate 9
    
    # Compression settings - use maximum compression for long retention
    compress
    compresscmd /usr/bin/gzip
    compressoptions -9
    delaycompress
    
    # Size-based rotation trigger for unexpected error spikes
    maxsize 50M
    
    # Always rotate even if small - errors are critical
    # (removed minsize to ensure rotation happens)
    
    # Handle edge cases
    missingok
    
    # DO rotate even if empty - maintains consistent schedule for compliance
    ifempty
    
    # Create new file with proper permissions
    create 644 www-data www-data
    
    # Use date extension for audit trail
    dateext
    dateformat -%Y%m%d
    
    # Copy and truncate to avoid losing any error messages
    copytruncate
    
    # Post-rotation script
    postrotate
        # Log rotation event for audit purposes
        echo "$(date): error.log rotated" >> /var/log/rotation_audit.log 2>/dev/null || true
    endscript
}

#============================================================================
# DEBUG LOG - Previously had NO rotation config!
# Low importance, 7-day retention sufficient
#============================================================================
/var/log/samples/debug.log {
    # Rotation schedule: Daily (5.3 MB/day)
    daily
    
    # Retention: 7 copies for 7-day requirement
    rotate 7
    
    # Compression settings
    compress
    compresscmd /usr/bin/gzip
    compressoptions -9
    # No delaycompress - debug logs can be compressed immediately
    
    # Size-based rotation trigger
    maxsize 20M
    
    # Minimum size - don't bother rotating tiny debug files
    minsize 100K
    
    # Handle edge cases
    missingok
    notifempty
    
    # Create new file with proper permissions
    create 644 www-data www-data
    
    # Use date extension
    dateext
    dateformat -%Y%m%d
}

#============================================================================
# SYSTEM LOG - Already configured, minor optimizations
#============================================================================
/var/log/samples/system.log {
    # Rotation schedule: Weekly (low volume)
    weekly
    
    # Retention: 4 copies (adequate for system logs)
    rotate 4
    
    # Compression settings
    compress
    compresscmd /usr/bin/gzip
    compressoptions -9
    delaycompress
    
    # Handle edge cases
    missingok
    notifempty
    
    # Create new file with proper permissions
    create 644 root adm
    
    # Use date extension
    dateext
    dateformat -%Y%m%d
}

#============================================================================
# GLOBAL DEFAULTS (can be placed in /etc/logrotate.conf)
#============================================================================
# These settings apply to all logs unless overridden:
#
# weekly              - Default rotation frequency
# rotate 4            - Default number of rotations to keep
# create              - Create new log file after rotation
# compress            - Compress rotated logs
# delaycompress       - Don't compress the most recent rotated log
# notifempty          - Don't rotate empty logs
# missingok           - Don't error if log file is missing
# dateext             - Use date extension instead of numbers
#============================================================================
EOF
